newsitem.title: USA: Refco buys N.Y.-based Forstmann-Leff Associates.
newsitem.headline: Refco buys N.Y.-based Forstmann-Leff Associates.

text.p: Refco Group Ltd, one of the world's largest futures and options brokers, said Monday it bought Forstmann-Leff Associates, a New York-based investment firm that manages $3 billion in U.S. equities for institutions.
Neither Refco nor Forstmann-Leff would disclose the terms of the purchase.
Chicago-based Refco, which has operations in 15 countries and is also a broker in the cash markets, said it formed a holding company, Leff International, of which Forstmann will be a subsidiary.

"We made a strategic decision to add this investment management expertise to our existing capabilities and broaden the range of products and services available to our global institutional client base," Tone Grant, Refco's president and chairman of Leff International, said in statement.
Bill Harnisch, president and chief executive of Forstmann-Leff, said he and his 50-person staff would continue to manage $3 billion in U.S. equities and about $700 million in two hedge funds.

Refco also hired a group of portfolio managers from Union Bank of Switzerland to manage fixed-income assets in a separate subsidiary under the holding company. Refco said the former UBS managers would have an emphasis on investment grade corporate securities and high-yield securities.
"We might have other asset management classes as well," Grant said in an interview. "We might have emerging markets, we might have mortgages, I don't know yet."

Donald Phillips, who recently raised $4 billion as a principal in financier Sam Zell's Equity Group, was named president of Leff International, Grant said. Phillips is a former chief investment officer of Ameritech Corp. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
